scope: Critical evidence index for four Perry Xie videos; summarizes creator statements and evidentiary limits. Raw captions remain private under raw/.

videos.title: how i made $200k in 30 days with shopify stores i built in 10 minutes.. (w/ claude ai)
videos.creator: Perry Xie
videos.brief_summary: Demonstrates a fast AI-assisted Shopify storefront build for a product selected before the video begins. The creator narrates competitor page research, Claude-assisted copy and Liquid customization, then states the product was preselected and directs viewers to his separate research tutorial. It demonstrates a workflow and edited interface, not an independently measured conversion result or the full product-selection method. The title’s $200k/30-day framing differs from the opening’s $197k/50-day and $143k/30-day self-reports.
evidence_limits: Auto-caption transcription may mishear and is not a substitute for exact on-screen text.
Creator demonstrations, revenue figures, and tool estimates are not independently audited by this review.

videos.title: here's how i find winning products that print $100k/month (100% hit rate so far lol)
videos.creator: Perry Xie
videos.brief_summary: Explains a discretionary screen: inspect long-running, active ads; assess cost, size/weight, multi-unit purchase potential, problem/market fit and competitor density; estimate a competitor’s revenue using traffic, assumed conversion and price; then consider bundles/free gifts. It demonstrates filters and one product/store example. Its 100% hit-rate title has no sample denominator, and the featured $138k/month figure is an assumption-based estimate rather than verified sales.
evidence_limits: Auto-caption transcription may mishear and is not a substitute for exact on-screen text.
Creator demonstrations, revenue figures, and tool estimates are not independently audited by this review.

videos.title: Speedrunning a $100k/month shopify store (w/ claude ai) pt.1
videos.creator: Perry Xie
videos.brief_summary: Applies the research framework to a grounding-sheet offer and builds a store quickly with AI and Atlas. It adds a 20-day native-ad filter recipe and discusses copying competitor structure, sourcing and page content. The video includes useful caution to substantiate health mechanisms and claims, while its revenue and hit-rate statements remain self-reported. It is a build demonstration; it does not show a full controlled ad test outcome.
evidence_limits: Auto-caption transcription may mishear and is not a substitute for exact on-screen text.
Creator demonstrations, revenue figures, and tool estimates are not independently audited by this review.

videos.title: Speedrunning a $100k/month shopify store (w/ claude ai) pt.2
videos.creator: Perry Xie
videos.brief_summary: Continues the speedrun series with long-form native ad construction, three desire-based ad sets and nine ad variants, then gives a brief day-one to day-three purchase/ROAS rule and 20% budget adjustment heuristic. A 3.39 ROAS/$400-spend day is presented as an example. The speaker says detailed performance evaluation belongs in another video, so this does not provide a complete or independently verified testing protocol.
evidence_limits: Auto-caption transcription may mishear and is not a substitute for exact on-screen text.
Creator demonstrations, revenue figures, and tool estimates are not independently audited by this review.

claim_audit.claim: Title: “$200k in 30 days”; opening says $197,000 in 50 days for one store and $143,000 in 30 days for another.
claim_audit.missing: The title and opening may describe different stores or windows, but the relationship is not explained; gross/net and source records are absent.
claim_audit.our_response: Preserve both as distinct creator claims; do not convert the title into an established result.

claim_audit.claim: The showcased process built the stores associated with $197k/50 days and $143k/30 days.
claim_audit.missing: No counterfactual, underlying financial records, store cohort or evidence that the website-building method caused those sales.
claim_audit.our_response: Treat the build as a tutorial, not evidence that a ten-minute AI site generates sales.

claim_audit.claim: Product was already selected before the store-build demonstration.
claim_audit.missing: The selection process is outside this demonstration.
claim_audit.our_response: Use the dedicated research video for the filter; don’t claim the main tutorial tested product discovery.

claim_audit.claim: “100% hit rate so far” for winning products.
claim_audit.missing: No number of products/stores, definition of hit, failed attempts, observation period or independent record.
claim_audit.our_response: Do not infer probability of success or expected value.

claim_audit.claim: Filter: US, top two performance tiers, max five ads per brand, image, still running, runtime >=25 days.
claim_audit.missing: No validation that the tool’s tier or runtime measures profitability; output universe and number inspected are not recorded.
claim_audit.our_response: Report as a reproducible filter setup, not a proven winning-product predictor.

claim_audit.claim: Product screen values low COGS, small/light shipping, multi-unit potential, real problem and large TAM.
claim_audit.missing: No thresholds, weighting, scoring rule or evidence that each factor is predictive.
claim_audit.our_response: Use as prompts for due diligence and compare against actual sourcing/market evidence.

claim_audit.claim: Demo reports 105,000 visits across roughly three months, then increases the estimate without validation and chooses 60,000 monthly visits x assumed 3% conversion x $77 price. This implies 1,800 orders and $138,600 monthly revenue, narrated as about $138,000.
claim_audit.evidence_status: scenario arithmetic on estimated and assumed inputs; not observed sales
claim_audit.missing: The upward traffic adjustment, store-specific conversion, order count and product-price mix are unverified. The spoken revenue figure is approximate; 60,000 x 0.03 x 77 equals $138,600.
claim_audit.our_response: Preserve the creator's roughly $138k estimate alongside its assumptions; do not report implied orders as measured orders or revenue as verified sales.

claim_audit.claim: Calls product “untapped” after a keyword-based Meta Ad Library check appears to find one relevant seller.
claim_audit.missing: Search term, geography, recall, product synonyms and seller universe are incomplete; one recognized competitor does not measure all competition.
claim_audit.our_response: Say few direct matches were noticed in the shown search; avoid market-wide saturation claim.

claim_audit.claim: A minimum 25-day runtime is used to infer ads have enough data and may be winners.
claim_audit.missing: Ad duration can reflect many causes; no spend, impressions, purchases or profit evidence shown.
claim_audit.our_response: Use longevity as a lead for investigation, not success proof.

claim_audit.claim: In TrendTrack, speedrun part one uses active, minimum 20 days, image, US, English, ad-copy length >=1,000 (called words by the speaker) and ad-rank descending.
claim_audit.missing: The current filter unit was not independently checked. Length does not establish native format or profit, and 20 days differs from the July tutorial's 25-day recipe. The speedrun explicitly switches from GetHookd/Similarweb to TrendTrack.
claim_audit.our_response: Treat this as a historical creator-narrated discovery recipe; verify current units and tool behavior before reproducing it.

claim_audit.claim: Claims 100% hit rate across many stores, all with $100k+ in first month.
claim_audit.missing: No denominator, definitions, failures, costs, financial statements or external corroboration.
claim_audit.our_response: Do not transfer into a success-rate assumption.

claim_audit.claim: Day 1 purchase optional; day 2 aim for at least one purchase; day 3 seek purchases above break-even ROAS.
claim_audit.missing: No budget/exposure threshold, attribution, sample size, statistical rationale or definition of break-even margin.
claim_audit.our_response: Do not use as a spend authorization or universal cut rule.

claim_audit.claim: Creator reports a day-three snapshot of 3.39 ROAS on $400 ad spend.
claim_audit.missing: No independent account export, attribution detail, orders/refunds or contribution calculation. $400 is the cited spend at the displayed day-three checkpoint; the video does not establish it as a daily budget or the total cost of the full test.
claim_audit.our_response: Treat as an illustrative platform snapshot, not profit evidence.

claim_audit.claim: Raise campaign budget 20% at midnight above break-even; optionally another 20% if >2x break-even; reduce 20% after a 24h dip.
claim_audit.missing: No controlled comparison or exact dip threshold; ROAS alone may not capture contribution or delayed refunds.
claim_audit.our_response: Only an example of the creator’s operating rule; calculate business-specific break-even first.

claim_audit.claim: Near 30:35 to 30:54, creator gives a rough losing-test summary referencing below-break-even ROAS after days 3 to 5, testing “desire 4” and “desire 5,” no purchases, and says undelivered spend is not a test.
claim_audit.missing: Some wording is caption-uncertain; no reproducible spend threshold, exact stopping rule or completed test history.
claim_audit.our_response: Do not operationalize without source video inspection and a predeclared test plan.

claim_audit.claim: Description links TrendTrack discount, Atlas, Rapid Bundles, a private supplier and paid Luxury Tools; other videos also promote tools/Atlas.
claim_audit.missing: Affiliate/referral terms and commercial arrangements are not fully established in the reviewed captions/metadata.
claim_audit.our_response: Record commercial incentives as context; links alone do not show advice is false.
